title: Dissemination audit in full, and the poll-grid test
why: the audit was the paper's least documented contribution, reported as a median and a worst case, and a referee offered a poll schedule as an equally consistent explanation

source.note: committed per-file capture: one row per archived file, with its run, forecast hour, initialisation time, mirror write time and the derived lag

poll_grid_test.hypothesis: if the mirror wrote on a fixed polling cadence, lags would snap to multiples of the poll interval: few distinct values, evenly spaced by that interval
poll_grid_test.verdict: NOT consistent with a poll grid: the lags vary at second resolution within a band about a minute wide, which is what a real completion time recorded by a filesystem looks like and not what a poll schedule produces

what_the_timestamp_is: the mirror's file-write time, an UPPER BOUND on true dissemination completion. Every pre-gate classification is therefore conservative: a mirror write before the gate implies the feed delivered before the gate. The post-gate classification does not rest on this measurement -- the published specification is its source, and these timestamps corroborate it
